Linda McMahon: Parents' Right to Opt Out of AI
Evidence: parental choice, measurable outcomes, student agency

Education Secretary Linda McMahon argues parents must retain full authority to opt out of AI instruction if schools fail to prove tangible benefits.

On CNN's State of the Union, Education Secretary Linda McMahon stated parents have every right to withdraw students from AI teaching tools if positive outcomes are not demonstrated.

The Poison:
Giving parents opt-out rights preserves agency, but managing individualized non-AI curricula could strain underfunded public school staff.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
No plane switch detected. McMahon addresses the WHO (parents and students) rather than subordinating them to the WHAT (AI technology adoption).

Social Physics Analysis:
By establishing upfront transparency and placing the burden of proof on institutions, the policy preserves trust. Empowering parents to demand demonstrated value avoids coercive technological dependency.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
Mapping stated intent to structural reality shows steady alignment with parental empowerment and institutional accountability.

The Unavoidable Truth: Technology in classrooms must serve student outcomes rather than institutional convenience.
The Unavoidable Lie: Mandating automated instruction without consent guarantees educational success.

Alethekanon:
Placing the burden of proof on the school to show measurable value protects parental agency against unchecked technological creep.

Awwthekanon:
Children flourish when parents and teachers stay deeply connected, ensuring tools adapt to human needs rather than replacing genuine care.

Brothekanon:
If the robot tutor isn't actually helping your kid pass math, you should definitely be allowed to pull the plug.
